research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; current YE March 2026 offence composition, coverage, trend, data-quality and outcome-timing controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Knife homicide fall and historical low
verified_claims: knife or sharp instrument homicides fell 14% to 176 from 204
the count was the lowest since year ending March 1991 using broadly comparable Homicide Index data
limitations: the police recorded crime series and Homicide Index are not directly comparable

sources.name: Knife-enabled assault share
verified_claims: 44% of knife-enabled crimes were assault with injury or assault with intent to cause serious harm
limitations: the share describes offence composition, not local risk

sources.name: Knife-enabled robbery share
verified_claims: 39% of knife-enabled crimes were robbery offences

sources.name: Knife-enabled homicide share
verified_claims: 0.4% of knife-enabled crimes were homicide offences
limitations: a small share does not imply low severity

sources.name: MPS knife threat seen
verified_claims: 56% of Metropolitan Police knife-enabled offences involved a knife used to threaten and seen by the victim
limitations: the figure applies to Metropolitan Police records, not England and Wales as a whole

sources.name: MPS knife threat not seen
verified_claims: 19% of Metropolitan Police knife-enabled offences involved a knife used to threaten but not seen by the victim
limitations: victim belief and recording rules affect classification

sources.name: MPS knife injury share
verified_claims: 24% of Metropolitan Police knife-enabled offences involved the knife being used to injure the victim
limitations: the share is force-specific and not a parcel measure

sources.name: MPS extraction-date comparability
verified_claims: monthly Metropolitan Police knife totals may differ from official statistics because extracts are taken on different dates
limitations: edition and extraction date must be pinned before comparison

sources.name: Firearms lowest since 2015
verified_claims: firearms offences in year ending March 2026 were at their lowest level since year ending March 2015
limitations: historical comparisons remain subject to collection definitions

sources.name: Firearms peak comparison
verified_claims: 5,151 firearms offences in year ending March 2026 were much lower than the year ending March 2006 peak of 11,088
limitations: the comparison is descriptive and not adjusted for population

sources.name: Firearms collection use scope
verified_claims: the firearms series includes crimes where a firearm was fired, used as a blunt instrument, or used as a threat
limitations: mere possession offences are not necessarily included in this special collection

sources.name: Imitation firearm definition
verified_claims: imitation firearms include replica weapons and low-powered BB or soft-air weapons
limitations: imitation status does not mean the incident was harmless

sources.name: Other firearm categories
verified_claims: other firearms include CS gas, pepper spray and stun guns

sources.name: CSEW violence incidents
verified_claims: CSEW estimated 989,000 incidents of violence with or without injury
there was no statistically significant annual change
limitations: the interviewer-administered estimate underestimates domestic violence

sources.name: CSEW violence decade comparison
verified_claims: violence with or without injury was 33% lower than the year ending March 2016 estimate of 1.5 million
limitations: long-term comparison applies to the CSEW household population
